cross_references.note: Apportionment (§4663) applies to permanent disability indemnity, NOT to medical treatment. The employer's medical treatment obligation under §4600 is not reduced by apportionment — the employer must treat the industrial component regardless of the PD apportionment percentage.

§3202 liberal construction applies to ambiguities in §4663 — including what constitutes 'substantial medical evidence' for apportionment and what conditions qualify as causally contributing. Ambiguities resolved in worker's favor.

If the employer's QME engaged in systematic speculation-based apportionment as part of a fraudulent claims management scheme (UA342 identity replacement), the underlying misconduct may support a §4553 enhancement on the PD award. The §4663 apportionment is applied to the base PD; §4553 then increases the employer's share by 50%.

Workers comp permanent disability rating and SSA disability determination are separate systems. WC PD is based on the AMA Guides impairment model; SSA uses a functional capacity model. A WC apportionment finding does not control SSA eligibility. However, WC medical records are relevant evidence in SSA proceedings.

A QME physician who produces a speculative or fraudulent apportionment opinion — particularly if it causes the worker to lose a significant permanent disability benefit — may have independent malpractice liability. The standard for an adequate apportionment opinion (substantial medical evidence; specific causation) sets the care standard. CA_Medical_Malpractice_Litigator owns the malpractice track.
